input.args: Update docs/features/sessions.md and docs/adr/0001-keep-sessions-in-signed-cookies.md to reflect that larder/sessions.py now has a logout(member_id) function, added because a volunteer needed to end a member's session immediately after their phone was stolen while logged in. Implementation: sign() now embeds an "issued" timestamp (the last_request time) in the signed cookie body; logout(member_id) records an in-memory revocation time for that member; verify() rejects any cookie for that member issued at or before the recorded revocation time, so the stolen-phone's cookie stops working immediately while a later sign() (e.g. a fresh login) for that member works again. Known limitation to document: the revocation record is in-memory per web-server process, so with more than one server behind the load balancer (per ADR 0001's own context) a logout only takes effect on the server that handled it, and is lost on restart — unlike the cookie signing itself, this part is not shared across servers. Please update the "Known limits" section of docs/features/sessions.md (the current bullet saying larder cannot log out one member from the server is no longer accurate and needs replacing with the new, narrower limitation), and edit ADR 0001 in place per the docs-layout rule for an edited decision (keep number/title, update Consequences, and add a line to Options/Decision only if warranted) to reflect that per-member logout is now possible, with its new caveat. Keep changes minimal and consistent with the existing writing style of these two pages.

last_message:
Done. Summary:

- `larder/sessions.py`: added `logout(member_id)`. `sign()` now embeds an `issued` timestamp in the cookie body; `verify()` rejects any cookie for a member that was signed at or before their last `logout()` call. A fresh `sign()` after logout (e.g. a new login) works again.
- Updated `docs/features/sessions.md` and `docs/adr/0001-keep-sessions-in-signed-cookies.md` in place, since they explicitly documented per-member logout as impossible — replaced that with the new behavior and its real caveat: the revocation is in-memory per server process, so it's immediate with one web server but incomplete across multiple servers behind a load balancer (and lost on restart).

For the stolen-phone case right now: calling `logout(member_id)` ends that session immediately on whichever server handles the call. If larder runs more than one web server, confirm with whoever deploys it that this is a single-server deployment, or rotate `LARDER_SESSION_KEY` instead (logs out everyone, but is guaranteed to work everywhere).
